description: Ox and Goat compatibility in the Chinese zodiac: Liu Chong (six clashes), their Earth and Earth elements, yin-yang, and what helps the pairing.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Ox and the Goat are a Liu Chong (six clashes) pairing, with Earth and Earth as fixed elements (both earth). The Ox brings patience, diligence and steady strength and the Goat gentleness, creativity and empathy. The tradition reads these as themes to work with, not a verdict.

sections.heading: How the Ox and the Goat relate
paragraphs: With the Goat, the Ox tends to bring loyalty, patience and dependable practical support. It often becomes the steady centre of a household, quietly carrying responsibilities. With the Ox, the Goat tends to bring gentleness, creativity and emotional warmth to a relationship. It often makes a home feel beautiful and caring. What the Ox tends to value most in a partner is sincerity, steady effort and respect for promises once they are made. What the Goat tends to value most in a partner is gentleness, encouragement and emotional security. Tenderness, beauty and patient encouragement usually let a Goat blossom. Soft music, handwritten letters and unhurried weekends usually reassure a Goat.

On first meeting, the Ox often comes across as calm, reserved and quietly dependable. Meeting for the first time, the Goat often comes across as kind, gentle and artistic. Traditional readings associate the Ox with patience, diligence and steady strength and the Goat with gentleness, creativity and empathy. On the twelve-animal wheel the Ox and the Goat sit six branches apart, directly opposite each other. Opposite animals form the Liu Chong clashes, and the Ox and the Goat are traditionally described as strongly contrasting, sometimes magnetic, sometimes combative.

sections.heading: The traditional link: Liu Chong (six clashes)
paragraphs: The Ox and the Goat are a Liu Chong pair, one of the six clashes, sitting opposite each other on the wheel. Both have Earth as their fixed element, yet they are usually described as having very different temperaments: the Ox steady and practical, the Goat sensitive and imaginative. Traditional readings point to friction between duty and feeling, which can turn into balance when each values what the other offers.

Liu Chong, the six clashes, pairs each animal with the one directly opposite it on the wheel. Traditional readings treat these as the most challenging pairings, describing tension rather than impossibility, and many such couples are said to learn a great deal from each other. Each animal has exactly one Liu Chong partner, so for the Ox that partner is the Goat, and for the Goat it is the Ox. The Ox belongs to the Metal trine with the Snake and Rooster, and the Goat to the Wood trine with the Rabbit and Pig. In the traditional double-hour clock, the Ox names the hours from 1 am to 3 am and the Goat those from 1 pm to 3 pm.

sections.heading: Five elements and yin-yang
paragraphs: The Ox and the Goat share Earth as their fixed element. In five-element thinking that shared Earth is read as mutual recognition between the Ox and the Goat, with the caution that the Ox's and the Goat's excesses can double up as easily as their strengths. The Ox and the Goat are both Yin animals, so the Ox and the Goat share a more inward, receptive polarity. In five-element terms Earth is associated with stability and nourishment, a quality the Ox and the Goat hold in common.

In everyday terms, the shared Earth of the Ox and the Goat suggests stability, patience and practical care, with the caution that a steady Ox and a steady Goat can become set in their ways. Each birth year also carries its own element from the heavenly stems, so a Metal Ox differs from a Water Ox, and a Wood Goat from a Fire Goat; a full reading compares those year elements too. For example, the most recent Ox year, 2021, was a Metal year, and the most recent Goat year, 2015, a Wood year.

sections.heading: Needs, friction and what helps
paragraphs: With the Goat, the Ox usually needs sincerity, predictability and time to warm up, along with appreciation for its effort. With the Ox, the Goat usually needs security, encouragement and a partner who responds to its sensitivity with patience.

Under stress with the Goat, the Ox can become stubborn, silent or rigid, holding its position long after a compromise was possible. Under stress with the Ox, the Goat can become anxious, indecisive or withdrawn, and may feel criticised where none was meant.

What helps the Goat with an Ox is patience, clear commitments and raising changes early so it has time to adjust before a decision is needed. What helps the Ox with a Goat is steady reassurance, kind framing of feedback and shared creative or restful time.

After an argument, the Ox may need time before discussing it, and a Goat who waits patiently tends to get a sincere, considered answer. For its part, after an argument, the Goat usually needs reassurance that the relationship is safe, and an Ox who offers it warmly helps the Goat open up.

sections.heading: The Ox and the Goat day to day
paragraphs: At home, the Ox tends to maintain routines, repair what is broken and keep life orderly, valuing a Goat who respects its rhythms. Furniture lasts decades, recipes are perfected over years and repairs are done properly rather than patched. At home, the Goat tends to create a cosy, beautiful environment, appreciating an Ox who brings stability and gentle encouragement. Handmade touches, plants and a well-loved kitchen often mark a home the Goat has shaped. Embroidered cushions, watercolours and herbs on the windowsill are typical flourishes.

As a colleague, the Ox carries heavy workloads without complaint; beside the Goat, it offers persistence and an honest assessment of what is realistic. Long projects, quality control and steady delivery are where the Ox is usually most valued. As a colleague, the Goat contributes creativity and empathy; beside the Ox, it helps the team feel cared for and inspired. Design work, caring roles and creative collaboration are where the Goat's gifts tend to show. Shared projects that draw on the Ox's patience and the Goat's gentleness tend to show this pairing at its best.

faq.question: Are the Ox and the Goat compatible in the Chinese zodiac?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Ox and the Goat are a Liu Chong (six clashes) pairing. That describes a tendency, not a verdict; for the Ox and the Goat, the themes to watch are the Ox's stubbornness and the Goat's worry.

faq.question: What are the elements of the Ox and the Goat?
faq.answer: The Ox's fixed element is Earth (Yin) and the Goat's is Earth (Yin); in the five-element cycles, both earth. Each birth year adds a separate year element.

faq.question: Which San He trine do the Ox and the Goat belong to?
faq.answer: The Ox belongs to the Metal trine and the Goat to the Wood trine, so they are not trine mates.

faq.question: What might the Ox and the Goat enjoy doing together?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Ox usually enjoys steady, grounded pastimes such as gardening, long walks, home cooking and craftwork, while the Goat usually enjoys creative, soothing outings such as art classes, gardening, music and peaceful countryside walks. Alternating who chooses gives both a taste of the other's world.

faq.question: Does the Chinese zodiac use the calendar year?
faq.answer: No. Animal years begin at Lunar New Year: the Ox year of 2021 began on February 12 and the Goat year of 2015 on February 19, so January birthdays need checking. The calculator does this automatically.
